post.description:
Section 4.1: re-verify TOTP to mint a short-lived step-up cookie
that sensitive endpoints (transfer, escalation, disposal, ...) will
require once those endpoints exist (Phase 3+).

Generates a new TOTP secret but does not activate it yet — Section
4.1 enrollment is two-step (start, then confirm with a real code) so
a user can't lock themselves out by saving a secret they can't
actually produce codes for.

get.description:
Section 4.1: device/session list with remote sign-out. Scoped to
the caller's own sessions — there is no action in Phase 1's matrix
for viewing another user's sessions.

schema.title: Response List Sessions Api V1 Sessions Get

get.description:
Scope is enforced twice (Section 4.2 layers 1 and 3): `can()`
gates entry to the action at all, and Postgres RLS on `users`
(Phase 1 migration) independently filters which rows come back even
if this query forgot a WHERE clause.

For an OWN_BUREAU-scoped role, "list" means "list within my own
bureau" — resource_bureau_ids is the actor's own bureau_ids, which
trivially satisfies the intersection check in `can()`. Omitting this
(as a previous version of this endpoint did) makes `actor_bureau_ids
& resource_bureau_ids` always empty, silently 403-ing every
OWN_BUREAU-scoped role regardless of real bureau membership — found
via Phase 3's case-assignment dropdown, which depends on this
endpoint and was returning zero candidates for every bureau_head.

post.description:
Section 1.2/5: upload a CSV/XLSX, parse it, diff every row against
any existing institution (matched by permanent_id) — writes nothing
to `institutions` yet. A human reviews this preview and calls
POST /imports/{id}/commit to actually apply it (Section 1.4's
"human-validate before activation").

Applies every non-error row: creates institutions with
`status='pending_review'` (new) or updates the diffed fields
(existing) — these still require a separate `/institutions/{id}/verify`
before Section 1.4 considers them activated.

get.description:
Section 1.2: public reference data, readable by every
authenticated official (T1-equivalent — this is not case content).
Shows `pending_review` rows too, with their status visible, rather
than hiding import results until verified (Section 1.4's honest
empty/partial-state rule).

schema.title: Response List Institutions Api V1 Institutions Get

get.description:
Section 2.1 R2's consolidated case history, built on top of
Phase 3's `cases` table — T1 coordination metadata only (case ID,
matter type, status, handling bureau, date), the same boundary
`GET /cases` uses: this is exactly R2's "list of every case across
all bureaus the viewer may see", not case content. Was a hardcoded
empty stub through Phase 2/3 (Section 0 rule 2 — no fabricated
placeholder before cases existed); now real.

schema.title: Response List Aliases Api V1 Institutions  Institution Id  Aliases Get

post.description:
Storage only this phase — Section 8.1's resolver that actually
consumes aliases for matching is Phase 4 (docs/limitations.md).

get.description:
Unauthenticated on purpose: the TEST sandbox banner (Section
1.4(b)) must render on the sign-in screen too, before any session
exists.

Section 5/R3: "shows likely matches before the officer submits" —
every open (non-disposed) case already registered against this
institution, regardless of which bureau holds it. Advisory only:
the caller decides whether to proceed (Section 8's full overlap
engine with text-similarity scoring is Phase 4; this is the
same-institution hard match Section 8.3 calls INFO-level).

This is a pre-submission check, not scoped to a specific resource
bureau yet — for an OWN_BUREAU-scoped role it's "can I register at
all for my own bureau", so resource_bureau_ids is the actor's own
bureau_ids (self-scope). Omitting this makes the OWN_BUREAU
intersection always empty, 403-ing bureau_head/case_officer on every
registration attempt — found live via the case-registration screen's
duplicate-check call.

schema.title: Response Duplicate Check Api V1 Cases Duplicate Check Get

post.description:
Section 5/R3: every mandatory field is required by the schema
itself (FastAPI 422s on a missing one) — case ID, date of receipt,
nature/category, assigned Bureau/Cell are all set here; status,
last action, and expected disposal date are set by the projection
update, not hand-assigned (Section 6.3).

get.description:
Section 4.3 T1: coordination metadata, broadly visible to every
authenticated official — this is exactly what lets RB see PGRC is
handling the same institution (Section 5's core ask), without
exposing case content (that's `/cases/{id}/events`, Section 4.3
T2, bureau-restricted).

Section 9.7/R9's search/filter + Section 10's "keyset pagination
everywhere" — the previous build this is replacing returned
unbounded lists; this one caps at `limit` (default 50, max 200)
and returns `next_cursor` (the last row's `seq`) for the caller to
pass back, rather than an offset that drifts under concurrent
writes.

get.description:
Section 6.5: computed directly from raw rows every time (no
cached `dashboard_counters` yet — Phase 6) specifically so
tests/test_case_counters.py's reconciliation check has something
real to compare against: this function *is* the reconciliation
query.

Section 4.3 T2 / R8: the real content boundary. Only the handling
bureau and `competent_authority` see the timeline; everyone else
gets a 403, not a redacted version — Postgres RLS on `case_events`
(Phase 3 migration) independently enforces the same boundary even
if this check is ever bypassed.

metadata (see `Alert`'s docstring in app/models.py) — broadly
listable so `SLA_POLICY_MISSING` reaches `super_admin`, who has no

post.description:
Section 6.4(c): a one-time, 30 s, single-use ticket bound to the
user and an IP /24 prefix. A WS/SSE connection can't carry the
double-submit CSRF header a normal `fetch()` can, so the short-lived
ticket is the subscribe-time credential instead — consumed exactly
once, by `_consume_ticket`'s `GETDEL`.

get.description:
SSE fallback (Section 6.4(e)) for proxies that break WebSockets.
`Last-Event-ID`, when the browser's EventSource sends it on
reconnect, takes priority over the `since_seq` query param.

Section 6.5/9.6's Command Dashboard tiles — reuses `case:list`'s
permission (dashboard tiles are aggregates over the same T1
coordination metadata `GET /cases` already exposes to every
authenticated official, never case content), so there is no
separate `dashboard:read` action to keep in sync with it.

Section 9.7's "saved views" — personal to the caller (Scope.SELF),
same own-record pattern as `app/routers/sessions.py`.
